BEL.note: UN Comtrade/USDA 2024: Belgium is the world's #1 frozen-fry (HS2004.10) EXPORTER (~3.0 Mt of product), processing imported and home-grown raw potatoes through Clarebout, Agristo, Ecofrost, Lutosa and Mydibel. Tiny domestic consumption vs huge export surplus.

NLD.note: UN Comtrade 2024: Netherlands is the #2 frozen-fry (HS2004.10) EXPORTER (~1.9 Mt product) via Aviko, Lamb Weston/Meijer, Farm Frites. Re-exports some product across the EU; large net exporter of processed potato.

CAN.note: UN Comtrade/USDA 2024: Canada is the #3 frozen-fry (HS2004.10) EXPORTER (~1.5 Mt product), shipping mainly to the US (1,261 kt) plus Japan and Mexico. Home of McCain Foods, the world's largest fry maker. Strong net surplus.

USA.note: UN Comtrade 2024: US frozen-fry (HS2004.10) trade is two-way: ~1.1 Mt exports (Japan, Mexico, Korea, Philippines) but ~1.55 Mt imports, overwhelmingly from Canada (1,261 kt). Net IMPORTER of frozen product despite Lamb Weston/Simplot capacity, because of integrated North-American sourcing.

FRA.note: UN Comtrade 2024: France produces frozen fries (HS2004.10) but is a large net IMPORTER (~715 kt, mainly from Belgium 482 kt and the Netherlands) to meet foodservice demand. McCain and Lamb Weston operate French plants.

GBR.note: UN Comtrade 2024: the UK is one of the largest frozen-fry (HS2004.10) IMPORTERS (~886 kt), sourcing from Belgium (514 kt) and the Netherlands (335 kt) since limited domestic processing. Structural net importer.

DEU.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Germany both produces and trades frozen fries (HS2004.10); net IMPORTER (~449 kt in, ~306 kt out) within the dense EU processing network, buying from the Netherlands and Belgium.

JPN.note: UN Comtrade 2024: Japan is a major frozen-fry (HS2004.10) IMPORTER (~424 kt) with little domestic processing, sourcing from the US (269 kt), Belgium, Netherlands, China and Canada for its QSR sector.

BRA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Brazil is the largest Latin-American frozen-fry (HS2004.10) IMPORTER (~326 kt), buying from Argentina, Belgium, the Netherlands and Egypt. Domestic processing is growing but lags demand.

ITA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Italy is a large frozen-fry (HS2004.10) net IMPORTER (~402 kt) from France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and Austria for its foodservice market.

ESP.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Spain is a major frozen-fry (HS2004.10) IMPORTER (~388 kt) from Belgium, the Netherlands and France; Lamb Weston and others also run Spanish plants. Net importer of product.

SAU.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Saudi Arabia is the largest Middle-East frozen-fry (HS2004.10) IMPORTER (~292 kt) from Belgium, the Netherlands, Egypt, France and the US for its fast-food sector. Negligible domestic processing.

MEX.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Mexico is a large frozen-fry (HS2004.10) IMPORTER (~316 kt), supplied mainly by the US (184 kt), Canada (90 kt) and Belgium under USMCA-integrated foodservice supply.

ARG.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Argentina is South America's main frozen-fry (HS2004.10) EXPORTER (~165 kt), shipping to Brazil (145 kt) and Chile; McCain operates a large plant in Balcarce. Regional net exporter.

CHN.note: FAOSTAT 2024: China both makes and exports frozen fries (HS2004.10), shipping ~183 kt to the Philippines, Japan, Indonesia, Korea, Thailand and Malaysia. Growing processing base; modest net exporter in product terms.

flows.note: UN Comtrade 2024: US-reported imports from Canada 1,260.6 kt frozen fries (HS2004.10); FAOSTAT 1,274 kt agrees within 2%. The single largest frozen-potato flow worldwide.
UN Comtrade 2024: France-reported imports from Belgium 481.7 kt (HS2004.10); FAOSTAT 523.1 kt agrees within ~8%. Belgium is the world's #1 frozen-fry exporter.
UN Comtrade 2024: UK-reported imports from Belgium 514.2 kt (HS2004.10); FAOSTAT 522.9 kt agrees within ~2%.

rankings.note: Frozen fries (HS2004.10) plus potato flour/flakes (HS1105), 2024, kt of product. Exporters led by Belgium (world #1 frozen-fry exporter), the Netherlands, Canada and the US; Belgium+Netherlands together supply over half of internationally traded fries. Importers led by the US (almost all from Canada), the UK, France, Germany, Japan and Brazil. Figures from UN Comtrade 2024 importer-reported bilateral totals cross-checked with FAOSTAT 2024 and USDA FAS; seed-captured aggregates confirm this ordering.

companies.name: McCain Foods
companies.note: World's largest maker of frozen french fries and potato specialties as of 2024 (~1 in 4 of the world's fries; ~50+ plants). Private, revenue est. ~US$11bn. Trades frozen product (HS2004.10), not fresh potatoes.
companies.improve: Disclose frozen-product shipment tonnage by destination and contracted raw-potato volumes by origin; private accounts limit visibility in 2024.

companies.name: Lamb Weston
companies.note: Largest US frozen-potato processor and a global top-two fry supplier in 2024 (NYSE:LW, ~US$6.5bn FY2024 sales). Operates Lamb Weston/Meijer in the EU (NLD/BEL) and plants in China and Argentina; exports HS2004.10 to Japan, Mexico, Korea.
companies.improve: Country-level export tonnage for HS2004.10 not broken out in 2024 filings; would sharpen flow attribution.

companies.name: Aviko
companies.note: One of Europe's largest frozen-fry makers (part of Royal Cosun) as of 2024, anchoring Dutch HS2004.10 exports across the EU, UK and to Asia. Operates plants in the Netherlands, Germany, Poland and China.
companies.improve: Publish per-country frozen-product export volumes; cooperative reporting is aggregate for 2024.

companies.name: Clarebout Potatoes
companies.note: Among the largest Belgian frozen-fry producers in 2024, a core driver of Belgium's world-leading HS2004.10 export volumes to France, the UK, Germany and beyond. Private and family-owned.
companies.improve: Private firm; 2024 export tonnage by destination undisclosed and would improve flow sourcing.

companies.name: Agristo
companies.note: Major Belgian/Dutch frozen-potato processor (plants in Belgium and the Netherlands) supplying private-label HS2004.10 fries across Europe and to export markets as of 2024. Family-owned.
companies.improve: No public 2024 shipment data by country; disclosure would aid attribution.

companies.name: J.R. Simplot Company
companies.note: Major US frozen-potato processor and long-time McDonald's supplier as of 2024; produces HS2004.10 fries for North America and exports to Asia-Pacific. Private, with plants in the US, Canada, China and Australia.
companies.improve: Private company; 2024 export volumes by destination not published.

global.note: World frozen-fry and processed-potato (HS2004.10+HS1105) product, kt, 2020-2024. Estimates compiled from USDA FAS frozen-fry trade data and FAOSTAT 2024 processed-potato balances; world exports ~9.1 Mt in 2024, led by Belgium, the Netherlands, Canada and the US. Production dipped in 2022 with the European drought before recovering through 2024.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook processed-potato/foodservice growth applied to 2024 base; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6
